fetch stream object with explicit subgroup_id (flags=0x1f: subgroup_mode=0b11, group_id, obj_id and priority present). Draft-16 Section 10.4.4.1 requires the first object on a fetch stream to state every field itself, so bit 0x10 is set and the Publisher Priority is present rather than inherited from a prior object

fetch stream object with datagram forwarding flag (flags=0x5c: datagram, group_id, obj_id and priority present). Draft-16 Section 10.4.4.1 requires the first object on a fetch stream to state every field itself, so bit 0x10 is set and the Publisher Priority is present rather than inherited from a prior object

vectors.error_detail: unexpected end of input while reading request_id

vectors.description: fetch stream with Objects 0 and 1 of Group 5 carrying Prior Group ID Gap 2 and 3. The second object's flags (0x20) leave its Group ID, Object ID and Priority to the Object before it. Section 11.3: "A Group contains more than one Object with different values for Prior Group ID Gap." That makes the Track malformed (Section 2.4.2)
vectors.error_detail: two Objects in Group 5 carry different Prior Group ID Gap values

vectors.description: fetch stream with an object in Group 9 and then Object 0 of Group 10 carrying Prior Group ID Gap 1 (flags 0x2C; its Group ID field is 10). Section 11.3: "An endpoint receives an Object with a Prior Group ID Gap covering an Object it previously received." The gap covers Group 9, which this stream delivered first. Section 2.1: "The Object is known to exist. From this state, it can transition to not existing, but not vice versa." The two conflict, so whether the Track is malformed is ambiguous, and the decoder does not refuse this

fetch stream with Objects 8 and 9 of Group 3, the second carrying Prior Object ID Gap 1. The second object's flags (0x20) leave its Group ID, Object ID and Priority to the Object before it. Section 11.4: "An endpoint receives an Object with a Prior Object ID Gap covering an Object it previously received." Section 9.16.3: "Within each group, objects are sent in Object ID order; subgroup ID is not used for ordering." The gap covers Object 8, delivered just before. Section 2.1: "The Object is known to exist. From this state, it can transition to not existing, but not vice versa." The two conflict, so whether the Track is malformed is ambiguous, and the decoder does not refuse this

fetch stream with Object 0 of Group 1 carrying Prior Group ID Gap 2. Section 11.3: "An Object has a Prior Group ID Gap larger than the Group ID." That makes the Track malformed (Section 2.4.2), which an endpoint detects from this Object alone
vectors.error_detail: Prior Group ID Gap 2 is larger than Group ID 1

vectors.description: fetch stream with Object 1 of Group 3 carrying Prior Object ID Gap 2. Section 11.4: "An Object has a Prior Object ID Gap larger than the Object ID." That makes the Track malformed (Section 2.4.2), which an endpoint detects from this Object alone
vectors.error_detail: Prior Object ID Gap 2 is larger than Object ID 1

vectors.description: fetch stream with Object 0 of Group 5 carrying Prior Group ID Gap 1 twice. Section 11.3: "An Object contains more than one instance of Prior Group ID Gap." That makes the Track malformed (Section 2.4.2), which an endpoint detects from this Object alone
vectors.error_detail: an Object contains more than one Prior Group ID Gap

vectors.description: fetch stream in Descending Group Order with Object 0 of Group 10 carrying Prior Group ID Gap 2, then Object 0 of Group 9. Section 11.3: "An endpoint receives an Object with a Group ID within a previously communicated gap." Group 9 is within the gap Group 10 communicated. That makes the Track malformed (Section 2.4.2)
vectors.error_detail: Group 9 is within the Prior Group ID Gap 2 that Group 10 communicated
